articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts a missile as fighting rages in Yemen’s al-Jawf
articles.summary: Houthi-affiliated media report that seven people were wounded in strikes on the city of Hodeidah.
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen says air defences intercepted a Houthi missile, while fighting continues to rage along key fronts between the armed group and forces loyal to the internationally recognised Yemeni government.

Defences “intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile” targeting Saudi Arabia’s southern region, said coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki in a statement on Monday.

Earlier, he said defences destroyed a drone launched toward the southern region on Sunday evening.

Also on Monday, the Saudi Civil Defence authority issued and then lifted alerts warning of “potential danger” in the city of Abha, as well as the provinces of Khamis Mushait, Taif and Najran.

The authority warned residents against “filming, publishing or sharing information” related to missile and drone attacks.

In Yemen, a media outlet affiliated with the Houthi armed group, also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), reported that seven people were wounded in Saudi-led coalition air strikes on Hodeidah on the Red Sea coast.

Four people were wounded in the attacks on Ras Isa port dock, while three others suffered injuries in a strike on an oil company site in the governorate’s Bajil district, Houthi media reported.

There was no comment on the reports from the Saudi-led coalition.

The latest clashes come as Yemeni government forces keep up their campaign to regain positions from the Iran-aligned Houthis in the strategic northern governorate of al-Jawf.

Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said on Sunday evening that government forces conducted 1,272 “targeting operations” against Houthi fighters, fortifications and weapons supplies over 24 hours.

Operations are ongoing in al-Jawf, neighbouring Marib and al-Bayda to the south, added al-Nazili. Government forces killed roughly 500 Houthi fighters and destroyed or disabled nearly 170 vehicles, equipment or heavy weaponry.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims.

In southwest Yemen, the Houthis continue to besiege the city of Taiz, blocking the entry of food, fuel and medical supplies, in what authorities warn is a mounting humanitarian crisis.

Taiz Governor Nabil Shamsan has called for urgent help for the city’s deteriorating health facilities. He said 120 health centres have stopped operating and another 66 are close to shutting down since the Houthis cut off supply routes to the city in early October.

Nour al-Din al-Mansouri, a member of the committee facilitating the work of the Taiz Siege Affairs Office, told Al Jazeera that at least 23 trucks were damaged or overturned in the past two weeks while seeking alternative routes to Taiz.

The city is Yemen’s third-largest and home to about one million of the country’s roughly 43 million people.

Full-scale fighting reignited in Yemen in September, when the Houthis made crucial gains that tightened their grip on the Red Sea coast.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a campaign called Operation Dawn of Yemen last month to regain Houthi-held sites and restore government control over other territories held by the group, which seized the capital Sanaa in 2014.

articles.title: The Voice UK winner Cate McHugh says she wanted to be Taylor Swift growing up
articles.summary: Cate McHugh has gone from busking on the streets of Cardiff to winner of The Voice UK.
articles.body:
The winner of the Voice UK says she decided "I was going to be Taylor Swift" as a teenager after being given a guitar, before busking on the streets of Cardiff.

Welsh singer Cate McHugh was crowned the winner of the show on Saturday , after being mentored by "the legend that is Sir Tom Jones".

McHugh, from Llantwit Major, in the Vale of Glamorgan, said Sir Tom was so warm and supportive that it felt "as if you've known him for years".

One of the standout pieces of advice he gave to her early on was to focus on the story being told in the song, she explained.

McHugh said that when she found herself getting "a little bit flappy and excited" while rehearsing Sir Tom would say "nope, what's the story?", and urged her to focus on that and "stay true".

The 32-year-old, who began her career as a teenager busking under the watchful eye of her parents, said she and Sir Tom had "really lovely interactions and a lovely comfortable connection" and that it was "just an honour to be in his presence".

The final was a poignant moment for Sir Tom as it was his last appearance on the show, having been a coach on and off since it began in 2012.

He made headlines in September after revealing that ITV had "made the decision" to "fire" him from the show's coaching panel .

McHugh said that in the moments before she was announced as the winner, she felt "super peaceful because I was so happy with where I'd come" in the show.

The singer, who has a six-year-old daughter and a 16-year-old stepson, said she felt confetti on her shoulder and "opened my eyes and thought 'oh my God, they said my name'."

She said she wanted to thank her family, including her husband Nathan, for surrounding her with "all of that love" and support throughout the show and during the final.

Recalling her early days of performing, McHugh said "I was the kid who was always singing and my parents decided very early on that if they didn't put me in singing lessons this was going to get really annoying really quickly".

She was gifted an acoustic guitar for her birthday around the time Taylor Swift released her album Fearless, and "decided that I was going to be Taylor Swift, I was going to learn the entire album from start to finish".

Aged 15, she told her parents she wanted to busk in Cardiff and "they did everything they could to fulfil that happening in the safest way which did mean, apparently, my father was lingering around on Queen Street, just keeping an eye on me".

Busking and taking requests from passers-by helped her to gain confidence and she has "paid my dues since then", including singing on cruise ships, McHugh said.

McHugh said that navigating losing her sight aged 22 due to degenerative macular condition Stargardt disease had made her more determined to succeed.

She said music had "always been an outlet, emotionally, as so many musicians will say, but for me, when I'm on a stage singing and the lights are down on the audience, it's the one place that I don't think about my sight loss".

McHugh said that "as long as I know the words and I'm not trying to read them off an iPad then I'm absolutely there in that moment".

She described her sight loss as "just a small part of me, it's not who I am".

McHugh added that while many people with differences and disabilities sometimes felt they had to make themselves smaller "so that you don't become a nuisance to people", she chose "to find a way to take up space and be bigger and that's where music took me".

She is now working on her first original song in a studio which should be released "relatively soon, hopefully, fingers crossed".

Footage shared by McHugh on social media after her win showed her laughing and smiling with family and friends screaming in delight as they celebrated her victory at a watch party in Cardiff.

She has won a £50,000 cash prize and a recording contract, with her first ever single, a cover of The Beatles classic Blackbird, now released.

articles.title: Yankees' Jazz Chisholm Jr. receives 'frustrating' free agent prediction from ESPN
articles.summary: Chisholm may have hurt his free agent market.
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. wanted to become the second player in Major League history to record a 50-50 season.

He stole 41 bases but managed just 19 home runs in his second full season with the New York Yankees .

It appears the Yankees will be moving on from Chisholm this offseason, as the second baseman is now a free agent. New York did not extend him the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Monday evening.

"Extending the qualifying offer (a one-year, $23.15 million deal) would have seemed easy on paper, but it's unclear how much enthusiasm the Yankees have for Chisholm, and I'm also not sure how much other teams will be pounding the table, as baserunning-and-defensive-heavy WAR totals often don't get paid in free agency, and on top of that, his xwOBA was a career worst," ESPN's Kiley McDaniel wrote.

McDaniel projects Chisholm to sign a two-year, $46 million contract this winter, well short of what the left-handed hitter believes he's worth.

In February, Chisholm told NJ.com's Randy Miller that he was looking for $35 million per year for eight to 10 years.

"What did I tell you last year? $300 million? It's probably bigger than that now, probably $35 million." Chisholm told Miller.

Well, the left-handed hitter certainly won't come anywhere close to that in his career. Chisholm still provides value with power and speed, but the flaws in his game (swing and miss, lack of focus) are hard to miss.

$46 million is way less than what Chisholm is hoping for, but he may have to accept that he lowered his value with his unbalanced performance this season with the Yankees.

articles.title: Bride Goes Viral After Challenging Groom to Beat Her at Valorant Before Marrying Her
articles.summary: A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant before they could officially marry.
articles.body:
A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant before they could officially marry.

A video showing the couple facing off in Riot’s tactical first person shooter has racked up nearly three million views in just one day. In the clip, the bride — decked out in her wedding finery and delicate hair ornaments — takes virtual shots at her soon-to-be lawfully wedded opponent, who sits across from her while a group of friends and family look on in amusement.

While this is certainly a unique way to celebrate one’s nuptials, it isn’t totally out of the ordinary. In fact, pre-wedding challenges like these are actually part of Chinese culture. They’re called ‘door games,’ and they’re a playful, lighthearted way to prepare for the actual ceremony and following reception.

Traditionally, these are silly tasks organized by bridesmaids that the groom must successfully complete in order to ‘earn’ the right to actually marry his bride. They usually take place the morning before the wedding at the home of the bride’s family, and his groomsmen are often enlisted to help. It’s a symbolic way of making the groom ‘prove his worth’ before he takes the bride’s hand in marriage.

Door games can be anything the bridesmaids choose, really; according to China Insider, these generally involve tasks like eating unusual foods, athletic challenges like doing push-ups, or testing their knowledge with trivia. In this case, the bridesmaids decided to put his elite gaming skills to the test — and it went so viral that even the official Valorant Instagram account took notice.

“Wait, the wife is lowkey locked in,” it said in a comment.

“The problem is if he wins, she will remember it for life, and he would not hear the end of it, but if he doesn’t, it would be near impossible to find another gem like her,” one viewer joked, while another called it the true definition of “skill-based matchmaking.”

Even the CEO of pro esports team GAM commented, saying, “How do we sign her?”

This is the latest gamer wedding to go viral after a Pokémon fan was able to fund his wedding by selling a trio of rare Charizard cards that had been stored in his attic for a mind-boggling $44,000.

And in 2024, a streamer couple took social media by storm for their Black Ops 6-themed wedding that they held at the Call of Duty Next event in Washington, D.C. Now, that’s true love.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Lakers face Luka Doncic ‘malpractice’ warning as trade likelihood reaches 65%
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have been warned that failing to strengthen their roster around Luka Doncic would be a major mistake, with NBA insider Jovan Buha putt...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have been warned that failing to strengthen their roster around Luka Doncic would be a major mistake, with NBA insider Jovan Buha putting the chances of a trade at 65 per cent.

The Lakers have made an impressive 6-2 start to the season, largely thanks to Doncic's outstanding form. However, questions remain over their depth, particularly at centre and on the wing.

With the Western Conference looking increasingly competitive, Los Angeles could look to make additions before the trade deadline to improve its championship chances.

Jovan Buha says Los Angeles Lakers would be making a mistake by not trading

Speaking on his podcast, Buha's Block , the insider explained why the Lakers need to take advantage of Doncic's current form rather than leave gaps in the roster.

"If the Lakers don't make a move and don't try to improve this roster, it would be, to quote you, malpractice," Buha said. "I just think that would be a giant mistake having Luka in his prime, potentially the best season of his career, and to not improve a couple of holes in the roster."

Buha believes Los Angeles has a strong opportunity to compete in the West and should be prepared to act.

"Odds of making a trade, I would say like 65% right now," he added.

However, the insider does not necessarily expect the Lakers to make an immediate move. He suggested the franchise could wait until it has a clearer understanding of its rotation and where the biggest problems lie.

"If someone goes down, maybe there's a different need, or there's some urgency to do something, or if they just continue to struggle to navigate some of these bench groups, maybe they feel some urgency to get a center at some point in December," Buha said.

The Lakers have reportedly been looking for another centre to provide cover behind Walker Kessler, while an upgrade at starting forward is also among their priorities.

Doncic's form makes the situation particularly important. He is averaging 38.3 points, 8.1 assists and eight rebounds per game, putting himself firmly in the MVP conversation.

There is also a longer-term consideration. Doncic's current contract could run through 2028 or 2029, depending on his player option, and ESPN's Brian Windhorst has previously highlighted the importance of keeping the Lakers in a strong position to secure an extension.

For Rob Pelinka and the front office, the challenge is finding the right additions without rushing into a deal. But Buha's warning makes one thing clear: the Lakers cannot afford to waste Doncic's current form.

articles.title: Indonesian president’s chief of staff dismissed over alleged wiretapping
articles.summary: Gov’t says Listyo may have committed ‘treason’ after he is arrested and accused of wiretapping top officials’ phones.
articles.body:
The Indonesian president’s chief of staff has been fired for what the government says could be “treason” after he allegedly wiretapped phones with the help of two other serving police officers.

President Prabowo Subianto dismissed Listyo Sigit Prabowo on Wednesday, a day after police announced his arrest over allegations that he had illegally wiretapped phones belonging to several high-profile individuals, including the president and cabinet ministers.

Two other senior police officers were also arrested, including Ahrie Sonta Nasution, head of the legal division of the Indonesian National Police, according to local media.

“This was, of course, carried out by certain rogue individuals, and we are also of ‌the view that what was done may already fall into a category that can be considered an act tending towards treason,” presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi said on Wednesday.

“It also tends towards acts that endanger state interests and the safety of the nation’s leadership, including the safety of the head of state,” he said.

The unauthorised wiretapping allegedly took place from last year to this year while Listyo was serving as chief of the National Police, a position he held for five years before becoming the president’s chief of staff last month.

The suspects are also accused of trying to conceal their actions by ordering the deletion of files containing intercepted communications last month.

Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Indonesia’s senior minister for legal affairs, said the motive behind the alleged wiretapping has not yet been determined.

The operation was conducted “without any legal basis or without any investigative or inquiry process in accordance with applicable laws”, according to Asep Safrudin, the top detective in the National Police.

Also on Wednesday, the Indonesian military deployed more than 20,000 soldiers in the capital, Jakarta. It did not say whether the deployment was linked to the arrests.

The new deployments include marine and navy troops, as well as personnel from training centres and naval bases in Java and Lampung province.

Indonesian armed forces spokesperson Major-General Muhammad Nas said the troop movement was standard procedure for maintaining national security and territorial integrity.

“Troop deployments are a normal occurrence,” Nas said, adding that the military “must always be prepared to protect the entire nation and safeguard the integrity of the Republic of Indonesia”.

articles.title: Bruins' James Hagens Linked With Major Award After Hot Start to Rookie Season
articles.summary: Hagens leads all rookies in scoring. If he's able to maintain that pace through the end of the year, that should see him compete for the grandest honor a fir...
articles.body:
The Bruins are back where they belong, sitting just three points off the Hurricanes for first-place in the Eastern Conference. There are a host of players to credit for their surging start to the year. None are as young as James Hagens, however.

The newly-minted 20-year-old has been a key cog in Marco Sturm's lineup thus far, amassing the third-most points on the roster despite averaging the fifth-fewest minutes. Hagens is a star in waiting. Talking heads are starting to realize it, too.

Here's what you need to know about Hagens' hot start, including how it might land him in award contention come the end of the season.

James Hagens Linked With Major Award After Hot Start

Hagens placed third on the Daily Faceoff's Steven Ellis' Calder Trophy ladder. Ellis writes:

Hagens was a natural center throughout junior and college, but it's never easy for a young player to come in and take on the added responsibility as a rookie. So it's been nice watching Hagens thrive in a third-line role, where he has managed to put up 11 points through 15 games. That's about a 60-point pace, which would be the second-best output by a Bruins rookie of the 21st century.

Ellis cited Hagens' speed, two-way prowess and desire to carry the puck in the middle of the ice as reason for his early success. He ranks tied for first in goals, tied for second in assists and first in points among rookie skaters. He has also proven a formidable asset on Boston's power-play, anchoring a second-line unit that has helped the Bruins convert 20 percent of their opportunities with a man advantage.

Hagens trailed only Canadiens netminder Jacob Fowler and Red Wings winger Michael Brandsegg-Nygard on Ellis' list of Calder Trophy favorites through the opening fifth of the season. He has ample time to scale up that mountaintop — Hagens' two-way sensibilities should help him surge from his third-line post in the coming few months.

In other words, Hagens is already showing signs of stardom in his age-20 season. That could help him compete for some hardware very soon.

articles.title: Indy Showcase, new college volleyball event, to help kick off season in 2027. What we know
articles.summary: College volleyball continues to grow around the Circle City, and in 2027 it will bring a new event to the city that once hosted the Final Four.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — College volleyball is returning to Gainbridge Fieldhouse with a two-day early season showcase.

The Indiana Sports Corp. announced Wednesday evening that the Indy Showcase will feature a four-team event Aug. 28-29, 2027. Similar to the men's college basketball Indy Classic, the event will serve as a fundraiser supporting Sports Corp. missions, according to a release.

Indianapolis once hosted a Final Four in 1987 at Market Square Arena, and college volleyball returned downtown on Oct. 16, 2025 when Purdue beat Indiana in the Monon Spike Match , which drew 6,477 fans on a sectional volleyball night , no less. The explosion of college volleyball reaching the Circle City is perhaps not a surprise.

The inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament will be hosted at the nearby Fishers Events Center from Nov. 20-25.

"You can't keep up with the explosion right now that is volleyball," Purdue coach Dave Shondell said last season. "And I think that you, fortunately people in the media are finally getting behind it — whether it be TV or print or on the internet — but it's hard to keep up with all the things that are going on in the attendance records that are being broken. You watch it every night you want to on TV, so it's a great time to be in volleyball."

The Indy Showcase will have information at a later date about the four teams, match times and broadcast information. However, it will bring four matches downtown early in the season, a rising trend across the sport.

The AVCA First Serve Showcase has become popular with Big Ten members Wisconsin (in Milwaukee) and Nebraska being featured prominently. Other events have blossomed out of those successes, both in television viewership and attendance.

Consider Indiana played at the Broadway Block Party in Nashville this season, and Purdue played in the State Farm Volleyball Showcase at the Sanford Pentagon in South Dakota and the Paradise Invitational in the Bahamas. Both teams were part of the Big Ten/SEC challenge, too.

Aside from the college level, the Indy Ignite enter their third season as the state's lone professional volleyball team. They won the Major League Volleyball regular-season championship in 2026 and open the next season in January. The state also produces top talent for the college level through various high school and club programs.

Now, Indianapolis is getting involved with the Sports Corp. and its mission to make Indianapolis the women's sports capital of the world by 2050. Perhaps that means a Final Four in the near future.

articles.title: Major Australian retailer David Jones folds after 188 years in operation
articles.summary: The brand's 38 physical stores and online site will continue to operate while receivers review its operations.
articles.body:
David Jones, Australia's oldest department store chain, has gone into voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk.

It comes after years of financial struggles for the 188-year-old retailer - known locally as DJs - as customers desert traditional shops for online shopping.

David Jones's physical and online stores will continue to operate while receivers FTI Consulting review the company, said voluntary administrators McGrathNicol.

"David Jones is an iconic company and so many Australians have stories and memories of visiting DJ's stores," said its CEO Erica Berthold, adding the brand has a "well-developed plan" to "reset the business for the future".

Berthold thanked "customers, our team members and our partners for their continued support of David Jones through this period".

David Jones employs about 6,000 staff and has 38 physical stores, with 17 of those in Westfield shopping centres.

Hours before the board voted to go into administration, Scentre - which owns Westfield - said the retailer had not paid its rent for October and was "therefore in breach" of its tenancy agreement.

"We understand the current retail trading environment, rising costs, a significant and outdated retail footprint, and supply chain challenges have led to this point," said Christopher Hill from receivers FTI Consulting.

By appointing administrators and receivers, David Jones will get "breathing space" and a chance to restructure the business, Hill said.

For many Australians, David Jones - and its trademark black-and-white houndstooth design - represented luxury.

But its collapse signalled the "death knell" for the department store format, said Jana Bowden, who teaches marketing at Macquarie University's Business School.

"It was once the epitome of glamour shopping in Australia - the Aussie version of Harrods," she said, "a place you would go to see and be a part of the glitz and glamour, where you could marvel at all the premium luxury labels, and feel like you'd made it."

Visiting the flagship city stores in Sydney and Melbourne was also a ritual for many Australian families, especially to see the festive Christmas window displays.

"People would travel from hours away from the city just to see those windows and experience the magic," Bowden said, but in recent years, the brand had lost its shine.

"The city stores have retained their upper end airs and graces, but the suburban stores leave a lot to be desired – they're mundane, they lack excitement and there's definitely no glitz," she said.

During Queen Elizabeth II's first visit to Sydney in 1954, the then-27-year-old monarch attended a banquet dinner on the seventh floor of the Elizabeth St store, according to the Sydney Morning Herald.

articles.title: Why Connor McDavid’s contract negotiations sparked major NHL debate: How his $25 million Edmonton Oilers extension could shape the team’s salary cap, roster flexibility and Stanley Cup ambitions
articles.summary: Explore how Connor McDavid's two-year, $25 million contract extension with the Edmonton Oilers could influence the team's salary cap management, roster flexibility, and pursuit of the Stanley Cup. Discover the significance of McDavid's decision to prioritize team success over a larger contract, and what this means for the Oilers' future plans and NHL contract negotiations.
articles.body: One of the biggest talking points in the NHL was Connor McDavid’s contract negotiations, which led to the Edmonton Oilers captain signing a two-year, $25 million extension on Oct. 6, 2025. The superstar decided to stay at his current $12.5 million average annual value (AAV) through the 2027-28 season instead of going for a much bigger paycheck or long-term deal.The decision attracted attention because McDavid is widely regarded as one of hockey’s elite players and could have commanded a substantially larger contract. His shorter agreement also gives him an opportunity to reassess his future while allowing Edmonton’s management to focus on building a roster capable of winning the Stanley Cup.How McDavid’s $25 million deal shapes Edmonton’s title hopesMcDavid’s extension was notable not only for its total value but also for the message it sent about his priorities. The two-year agreement is worth $25 million, with an AAV of $12.5 million, matching the annual cap hit of his previous eight-year contract.At the time of the announcement, the deal was viewed as a significant financial concession compared with what a player of his standing might have sought on the open market. McDavid could have pursued a longer agreement with a higher annual value, but he chose a shorter commitment that keeps his championship ambitions with Edmonton at the center of the discussion.Why Connor McDavid took a shorter dealMcDavid's decision demonstrates how much he values winning a Stanley Cup with Edmonton. The Oilers made it to the Stanley Cup Finals in 2024 and 2025, only to lose both times to the Florida Panthers. A shorter extension allows the organization to keep working towards the championship goal without tying up a big chunk of its future salary cap on one player for a few more years.The agreement also gives McDavid more control over his next career decision. Rather than committing to an eight-year deal, he has kept the possibility of testing unrestricted free agency after the 2027–28 season.This arrangement creates a different kind of pressure for both the player and the organization. McDavid has committed to two more seasons, while Edmonton must demonstrate that it can use its available resources to build a championship-caliber supporting cast.How Connor McDavid’s contract affects Oilers roster flexibilityThe financial structure of McDavid’s extension gives Edmonton a predictable $12.5 million annual cap charge for both seasons. That figure is important because the NHL salary cap limits how much a team can spend on its active roster. Keeping McDavid’s cap hit unchanged gives general manager Stan Bowman more room to manage contracts involving other key players.McDavid’s agreement is particularly significant alongside the contracts of Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard. Draisaitl signed an eight-year extension carrying a $14 million AAV, while Bouchard's contract also represents a major commitment to the Oilers' defensive core. The front office will have to plan carefully in managing those salaries, and McDavid’s deal.The organization has also tried to retain key defensive pieces. Jake Walman signed a seven-year extension in October 2025 worth $49 million and carrying a $7 million AAV. Edmonton then extended veteran defenseman Mattias Ekholm for three years at $12 million. Those kinds of deals show the team’s effort to keep continuity around its top players.What matters is the difference between McDavid's actual annual salary and his cap hit. His cap charge remains $12.5 million in both seasons, even though his signing bonuses and base salary are distributed differently. The contract also includes a full no-movement clause, giving him protection against being traded or moved without his consent.Why the Oilers must balance their championship rosterMcDavid's decision does not automatically guarantee that Edmonton will have enough room to sign every player it wants. The club still needs to consider contract renewals, player development, defensive depth and goaltending when planning its roster.However, retaining the captain at the same AAV provides a more predictable financial foundation than a substantially larger contract might have offered. It also allows the Oilers to keep investing in players who can contribute alongside McDavid and Draisaitl.The challenge for Bowman is to make those resources count. Edmonton has reached the Stanley Cup Final in consecutive seasons, but maintaining that level requires more than relying on its two leading forwards. Defensive consistency, reliable goaltending and contributions from the supporting lineup will all remain important.What Connor McDavid’s 2028 free agency means for EdmontonOne of the most significant aspects of the extension is its limited duration. McDavid's agreement runs through the 2027–28 season, after which he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent in 2028 at age 31.This gives the Oilers a defined period to demonstrate that their roster can compete for the championship. Should Edmonton show measurable progress, the organization may have the opportunity to negotiate another deal with its captain before he becomes an unrestricted free agent.The short-term nature also benefits McDavid by keeping his options open for negotiations. The NHL salary cap is going to keep moving, and a higher ceiling could open up opportunities for bigger contracts down the road. That does not guarantee that McDavid will leave Edmonton or sign a particular deal, but it gives him the freedom to evaluate his options when the current extension expires.What McDavid’s next contract could mean for the NHLMcDavid's decision has also raised questions about how superstar contracts influence negotiations across the league. His $12.5 million AAV is below a number of other top NHL players who have signed big deals, including Kirill Kaprizov’s $17 million AAV and Draisaitl’s $14 million AAV.His agreement is unusual because elite players usually have strong financial incentives to secure the maximum possible contract value. However, McDavid's situation also demonstrates that a player can prioritize team-building flexibility and a shorter commitment when considering his next career move.The Edmonton Oilers’ short-term goal remains the same: leverage their championship experience to win a Stanley Cup. McDavid has given management a solid cap number for two more seasons, but it is now up to the organization to build a competitive roster around him.At the end of the day, the extension is more than a $25 million deal. It’s a mutual commitment to another shot at a championship, while leaving the door open on McDavid’s longer-term future. articles.title: MLW owner talks Tessa Blanchard, Masha Slamovich signings: 'I believe in forgiveness'
articles.summary: Major League Wrestling owner Court Bauer says Tessa Blanchard's arrival was a decade in the making after a 60-day delay pushed her debut to the PPV.
articles.body: It’s no secret Major League Wrestling (MLW) has brought in some big names into the company over the last few years with wrestlers like Killer Kross, Scarlett Bordeaux, Austin Aries, Trevor Lee, Shotzi Blackheart and several others being on the roster at one point or another. Two other notable names that caught the attention of the pro wrestling world this year bolstered MLW’s women’s division – Tessa Blanchard and Masha Slamovich (known in MLW simply as Masha). CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE Blanchard, a third-generation pro wrestler, has vehemently denied racism allegations for years even as she’s been featured as a top player in several promotions. Slamovich addressed domestic abuse allegations in September 2025, apologizing for her actions in what she described as a "mutually destructive relationship." MLW first announced Blanchard’s signing in September of this year and she was initially planned for Fightland. Some confusion pushed back her debut to Saturday Night SuperFight, which takes place this weekend and can be seen on Veeps. MLW owner Court Bauer addressed Blanchard’s signing in an interview with OutKick Dropkick. "There are things in this business that happen that are just unique and I really can't talk about it other than saying, ultimately what happened was you had about a 60-day delay on it and instead of her debuting in Charleston for a TV taping, she's arriving at our pay per view, which is a critically awesome moment for it to happen. So, it worked out pretty damn good for us and we're thrilled, CMLL's thrilled and Tessa's thrilled. I think that's all that matters. "But for Tessa, she's been an incredible part of the CMLL roster, and for her to come over is a huge honor and she was actually supposed to be a part of the original relaunch of MLW in 2017. We had taped stuff of her training and, again, it was one of those weird things where just the timing didn't work and it didn't happen. She was gonna be like one of the cornerstones of MLW at that point in time of our new era talents. And then here we are. That was 2017. Here we are 2026, end of 2026, almost 10 years later. And seeing all of this incredible success she's had in Mexico and she's had elsewhere and it's to come back and do this finally. It's about a decade in the making. So finally, it will not be denied, just like her undeniable. she's gonna be here." Bauer told Wrestling Observer Radio he was a believer in "second, third chances" for people. OutKick Dropkick asked Bauer if he share the same sentiment for Slamovich. MLW'S COURT BAUER TOUTS 'HUGE YEAR' FOR COMPANY AMID MEDIA DEALS, SPLASH MOVES "I believe in forgiveness," he said. "As a Christian, I believe in forgiveness. I think we're so quick to condemn and everyone gets executed and then they're just on the island of irrelevancy. They are to be forgotten. They are shunned forever, and there are definitely people in this world, in this business, that should be. And there's people in this business that could be, but there are a lot of people that make bad mistakes, terrible mistakes, and they repent, and they realize their errors and their things that they could have done differently. They're young people, they're living in a time where they're just on the go constantly, and then they get to settle down and they get to have perspective. But you gotta have the ability to see that and then you have a conversation with those folks, you see where they're at, and I'm not saying one person in particular, but my approach has always been, yeah, you know, give second chances, give forgiveness. "I mean, we're so easy to condemn and I think that's just something that if I hadn't had a second chance, third chance, fourth chance, I mean I really sometimes would make a mess when I was younger and you don't realize, you know, maybe this is it for me and thankfully people gave me another chance, and if they hadn't, I wouldn't be here. I wouldn't be in this position, and I'm grateful for that. "And so forgiveness to me is like one of those things that really I wish would get an equal amount of enthusiasm, especially on social media, versus quick to just let's go out there and let's get our pitchforks and torches and go burn that person down. And once they're torched, they're satisfied and that person's just devastated. Yeah, maybe rightfully, they should be in that moment, on a sabbatical, but let them, you know, it's not all or nothing. I think there's a little bit of nuance there, a little bit of gray area in there, and I think that's where it's important to like let them kind of go on their journey of realizing that and then see if there's a conversation we had when the timing is right, when it's appropriate. That's kind of how … I've never really spoken about that deeply, but that's really where I stand both my heart and in my mind about it." Blanchard and Slamovich will both be in action at Saturday Night SuperFight. Blanchard will square off against Keyra and Slamovich will take on Zamaya this weekend. articles.title: G2 Esports Parts Ways With Head Coach Luka 'Perkz' Perković After His 'Tweet Bomb' Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach, Luka "Perkz" Perković, following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.
articles.body:
G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach and retired League of Legends player Luka "Perkz" Perković following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.

The 2,676-word-long tweet was published on November 4, 2026. Perković described it as his “first and last honest post in [the] last decade,” where he could “address some things honestly.” He explained that he’d written the statement to clarify his stance on certain topics “so that, at the very least, you can hate me for what I really stand for, and then that's completely fine by me.”

In the post, which he jokingly called a “tweet bomb,” Perković said he is not a fan of and does not endorse the Tate brothers in any way; claimed that “doesn’t really do politics” and has never “ever voted once” in his life; said he is not a fan of either Donald Trump or Kamala Harris; said he is a devout Catholic; denied being a “Putin fanboy” or being on the side of Russia in the war on Ukraine; and shared his stance on abortion, comparing it to “murder.”

“I don’t really do politics, nor have I even ever voted once in my life. I do have opinions, and I wish I was more educated on the topic, but the truth is I’m not, so I stay away from it,” he wrote. “There are some things I stand for, very simple things in life, but the only thing that is unshakeable for me, how it’s so widely accepted in public, is abortion. I cannot comprehend how people do not understand that is a muder, as life is created at conception. That is one view I will die by and never change.”

Perković also addressed his relationship with retired League of Legends pro and former G2 CEO Carlos "ocelote" Rodríguez Santiago, who stepped down from the company in 2022 after sharing a video of himself at a party with Andrew Tate. “Me standing up for Carlos publicly when he was being cancelled has nothing to [do] with all the things I’m all accused of supporting. Trafficking? Misogyny? Nazism? War? Are you okay?” Perković said of the matter.

“Carlos believed in me when nobody else did. I did not have a close relationship with my family when I was 16, including my parents, [who] I was not too close with, either. …Carlos and I have gone both completely different ways. He is his own person and I’m completely my own. In the end Carlos’ ego is something that put an end to his esports career, which was f**king insane. So there is a lesson to be learned in there, as well. We have a lot of different views on life.”

Perhaps the biggest takeaway from Perković’s post was his stance on abortion. This particular remark was a main talking point among fans and fellow players on social media, sparking a massive wave of backlash against him. G2 Esports addressed the situation in a public post mere hours later, where they confirmed that they have parted ways with Perković due to his tweet.

“Last night, like many of you, we saw the statement shared by the Head Coach of one of our teams. G2 is a diverse and international organization with different people from all around the world. While the world is complex and not everyone agrees on everything, some of the statements made last night do not align with G2's stance and values. We have fans with different cultures and personal opinions, and it is of the utmost importance to us as an organisation that we respect and uphold this diversity when representing G2. We acknowledge that this statement hurt many of our fans, and we want to apologize for it.

“As a result, we have decided to terminate our collaboration with the individual. We will now focus on rebuilding our staff and roster for the next season and ask for your patience, as we will not be able to communicate any changes until free agency officially opens. - Alban Dechelotte, CEO of G2.”

Perković has since published one other tweet — a Bible verse from Luke 6:22. “Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake,” he wrote. This post, too, has received backlash from users. Perković has not posted anything else on his account at the time of writing.

articles.title: MLW's Killer Kross faces biggest challenge yet as he defends world title against Josh Bishop at major PPV
articles.summary: Killer Kross says retaining his MLW World Heavyweight Championship against Josh Bishop at Saturday Night SuperFight comes down to toughness.
articles.body: Killer Kross will enter Major League Wrestling’s (MLW) Saturday Night SuperFight having to defend his MLW World Heavyweight Championship against Josh Bishop, who is riding a wave of momentum going into the pay-per-view. Kross and Bishop will meet in a Last Man Standing match at Cicero Stadium in Chicago. It will be Bishop’s best chance at dethroning Kross, who has been the champion since Battle Riot VIII. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE "I think I’ve got a very good chance to retain," Kross told OutKick Dropkick. "However, I think it's gonna come down to who's gonna come out of this the toughest. If you're not coming in, as close to bulletproof as possible, I don't think we're gonna be able to walk out the winner on this one. Last man standing, you know what I mean? It's. This isn't about wrestling ability, this isn't about technical prowess. This is gonna be who's tougher. That's just the way I see it." Last Man Standing matches turn out to be one of the more brutal showcases in pro wrestling. The object is to do enough damage to your opponent that he is on his back for at least 10 seconds. Kross, himself, is coming off a title defense against Donovan Dijak on the go-home episode of "Fusion." Bishop and Dijak broke apart and Bishop delivered an Exit 187 to Dijak, seemingly building momentum to the championship fight. MLW'S COURT BAUER TOUTS 'HUGE YEAR' FOR COMPANY AMID MEDIA DEALS, SPLASH MOVES But that was just a part of Kross’ 2026. He admitted the year has been "painful" but also highly successful. "I never doubted it," he said of the success he’s had this year. "But with pro wrestling, it doesn't matter really what you're capable of or what you think you can do and oftentimes, it doesn't even matter, depending on what company you're in, what sort of connection you have with the audience, if they don't want to give you the time to go out there and shine, then it's kind of like it doesn't exist. "So, tthe only thing that was up in the air was like once I get out here, are those opportunities gonna be available because I'm ready to deliver? And they have been in mass quantity. So, I mean, it's, I'm having the time of my life. I can't say it enough, man. I really, truly am." Despite the feud between Kross and Bishop this year, Kross recognized how far Bishop has come in his growth as a pro wrestler. "He has a bright future ahead of him," Kross said. "I've said it before and I'll say it again, he's a perfect throwback. He's got that Sid Justice, Sid Vicious type of demeanor, and people love that, and you just can't find those types of wrestlers sitting around anymore. "A lot of what we see in the programming is this incredible hybrid Lucia type stuff. The era of the big man is kind of few and far in between, and I think with wrestling being best formatted as a variety act, you gotta have somebody like that on the show. You need some, you need some heavy hitters, those larger than life type characters, and I definitely think he fits the bill." articles.title: Tornados atingem cidades do Rio Grande do Sul e deixam bairros destruídos | G1
articles.standfirst: Ventos provocaram danos em Santo Augusto e Palmeira das Missões; granizo atingiu Bento Gonçalves e temporais causaram estragos também no Paraná e em Santa Catarina.
articles.summary: Ventos provocaram danos em Santo Augusto e Palmeira das Missões; granizo atingiu Bento Gonçalves e temporais causaram estragos também no Paraná e em Santa Catarina.
articles.body:
Dois tornados atingiram neste sábado (7) o noroeste do Rio Grande do Sul. Centenas de casas ficaram destelhadas.

O temporal na cidade de Santo Augusto começou por volta de 1h30 da madrugada. Primeiro veio o vento forte e, depois, a chuva.

"Veio um raio logo em seguida com trovão, que a gente já sabe que foi muito próximo, um clarão mesmo, aí o vento forte, e a gente escuta como se fosse pedra de gelo, mas na verdade já era a placa da telha arrancando", conta Thales Costa.

Parte da casa do Maurício Dias desabou sobre ele. "Eu estava dormindo e acordei com aquele barulho. Quando vi, deu aquele estouro violento, arrebentou a janela e tudo caiu por cima de mim", diz.

"Eu tive que ir ao hospital e precisei fazer sete pontos. O corte foi muito profundo. Mas eu agradeço a Deus por estar vivo".

Cerca de 100 casas foram danificadas, algumas com o telhado completamente destruído . Os moradores trabalharam para consertar os estragos. O vento deixou ao menos três bairros destruídos.

"Foi um evento contínuo, com ventos que caracterizam tornado, até pela destruição. Eu tô com 28 anos de serviço nessa área e esse ano está sendo um ano bem atípico. A cada 15 dias está tendo um problema no estado", aponta o Major Silvano Oliveira Rodrigues, da Defesa Civil do estado.

Outro tornado também atingiu Palmeira das Missões, a 60 quilômetros de Santo Augusto. Um galpão de fertilizantes ficou destruído.

Em Bento Gonçalves, na Serra Gaúcha, pelo menos 1.500 casas foram danificadas pela queda de granizo durante a madrugada .

Prefeitura, bombeiros e Exército distribuíram lonas para os moradores, que passaram o dia consertando os imóveis.

Também voltou a chover forte nos outros estados do Sul do Brasil. Um temporal com ventos de mais de 70 quilômetros por hora arrancou o forro deste posto de combustível em Curitiba. Ninguém se feriu.

A ventania derrubou dezenas de árvores, algumas sobre a rede elétrica. 52 mil imóveis estão sem luz. Em todo o Paraná, são mais de 400 mil.

Mais cedo, em Santa Catarina, uma tempestade alagou a cidade de Abdón Batista, meio-oeste do estado.

Moradores precisaram de ajuda pra sair das casas. Na área rural de Papanduva, no Norte, a correnteza levou uma ponte.

articles.title: Claudio Castagnoli Calls League of Legends ‘the Best Sport to Watch’
articles.summary: Claudio Castagnoli didn’t start playing League of Legends until a showmatch crossover between his former company (WWE) and Riot Games introduced him to it.
articles.body:
ALLEN, Texas — Finding new hobbies can be difficult, especially when you're on the road for 300-plus days a year.

Pro wrestler Claudio Castagnoli has always liked gaming. Still, he didn't start playing League of Legends until a showmatch crossover between his former company (WWE) and Riot Games introduced him to it.

It's been eight years since that showmatch, and a lot has changed.

He works for a new company (All Elite Wrestling) and doesn't have enough time to play as many games as he'd like.

But he still finds time to watch League of Legends, including stopping by the World Championship quarterfinal match between Korea's T1 and France's Karmine Corp.

"League of Legends is the best sport to watch," he said. "It's so exciting."

Castagnoli appeared on the live broadcast, where he announced the teams as they entered the arena and was also interviewed.

For him, the chance to see the League of Legends World Championships is too good to pass up. Despite his world travels this year, including Mexico, the United Kingdom, and Japan, he hasn't been to Korea to soak up the heart of esports.

"I'm sure [League of Legends is] kind of popular over there," Castagnoli said with a smirk.

He compared the League of Legends crowd at the event to the rabid fans who attend AEW shows. He's been to a League of Legends event in China and said the experience is similar to the events he works.

"It's the passion of the fans for the team, for the game, and how they show it," Castagnoli said. "They have signs. They come early. They dress up. They wear jerseys. They show their passion and pride."

More importantly, he compared the title and pro wrestling as two industries that have immense lore and histories that fans can track for years.

Take weekly AEW television and the stories that advance week to week, and compare it to traditional media such as Arcane . Both build character lore and offer ways to attract fans while providing more content.

The thing, however, he said that was also similar was the idea that all it takes is exposure to the game and environment to get people hooked.

"There are a lot of people that are like, 'I'm not really into it,'" Castagnoli said. "I'm like, 'Well, if you come to a live show, you'll be a fan just because you see it.' Once you play, and I feel like, especially once you play with your friends, it just becomes so much more fun because we can all watch Worlds at the highest level."

He also offered advice to new League of Legends fans.

"Don't try to imitate because it's quite frustrating," Castagnoli said.

While Castagnoli can make physical feats seem effortless, such as his trademark giant swing, micro movements with a mouse and maneuvering around the Rift (the name of League of Legends' map) offer a different challenge.

"I'm the worst. I misclick and click the wrong buttons," he said. "My timing in that and in the ring, you think would match, but it absolutely doesn't."

Even though Castagnoli hasn't been as visible as he can be in the League of Legends space, he knows if and when he gets back to it, he'll be welcomed.

"I feel very grateful for the League fans because they're out there and they welcome me," he said. "I feel like it was a positive response [when I introduced the teams]. It's very cool."

articles.body: For many families, Diwali is a time to come together, light diyas and celebrate with loved ones. For the family of Captain Amit Bhardwaj, however, the festival carries a heartbreaking memory of a promise that remained unfulfilled. During an interview on the Zahra Jani Show, retired Indian Army officer Major Mohini Garge-Kulkarni recalled the story of Captain Bhardwaj and a letter he had written to his mother around Diwali. In the letter, he reassured her that he would return home and celebrate the festival with the family the following time.But that next Diwali never came for him. Captain Bhardwaj was killed during the 1999 Kargil War, leaving behind a family whose wait to welcome him home would never end. His story is a reminder that while soldiers guard the country during festivals, their families often celebrate with an empty place at the table and the hope of seeing their loved ones again.A Diwali letter filled with a promiseAs recounted by Major Mohini in the interview, Captain Bhardwaj had written to his mother during Diwali, promising that he would be home for the next celebration. Like many soldiers posted away from their families, he could not be certain when he would get another opportunity to return. For his mother, those words may have offered comfort and something to look forward to. For a family waiting for its son, even a simple assurance of a future reunion can carry immense meaning.However, the promise remained unfulfilled. Captain Bhardwaj lost his life while serving in the Kargil sector in May 1999, before he could return home for another Diwali. The story, shared years later by Major Mohini, brings attention to an aspect of military service that is not always visible in accounts of courage and battlefield operations: the emotional uncertainty experienced by soldiers' families.Who was Captain Amit Bhardwaj?Captain Amit Bhardwaj was born on March 4, 1972, in Jaipur, Rajasthan. He was the son of O. P. Sharma and Sushila Sharma and served with the 4 JAT Battalion of the Jat Regiment. According to his profile on Honourpoint, he joined the Indian Army in 1997 and was later posted to the Kargil region. During Operation Vijay in 1999, he became part of an operation that would cost him his life.On May 17, 1999, Captain Bhardwaj led a patrol towards Bajrang Post in the Kaksar sector. The mission was connected to the search for a missing patrol led by Captain Saurabh Kalia, whose team had come under enemy fire. Bhardwaj volunteered to lead the search party, driven by concern for his fellow soldiers. He was killed during the operation. His sacrifice became part of the larger story of the Kargil conflict, in which Indian soldiers fought under extremely difficult conditions to defend the country's territory.A soldier's sacrifice and a family's unending waitCaptain Bhardwaj's death was not only the loss of a young Army officer. It was also a personal tragedy for the family that had waited for his return. According to an account shared by his sister, Sunita Dhonkaria, his body was recovered 56 days after his martyrdom and brought home on July 15, 1999, wrapped in the Tricolour. The family later established the Shaheed Amit Bhardwaj Memorial Charitable Trust in his memory. His contribution has also been formally remembered in Kargil. In October 2024, Kaksar Bridge was renamed Captain Amit Bhardwaj Setu in his honour. His sister attended the ceremony and inaugurated a memorial dedicated to him.Why his story continues to touch peopleMajor Mohini's account of the Diwali letter shifts attention from the battlefield to the home a soldier hopes to return to. It reminds people that behind every uniform is a family waiting for a phone call, a letter or the chance to celebrate together again. For soldiers, missing festivals can be part of the demands of duty. For their parents, spouses and children, however, every celebration away from them can bring both pride and longing.Captain Amit Bhardwaj's promise to return for the next Diwali was never fulfilled. Yet, his story continues to be remembered through his family's efforts and the tributes paid to his service. The diyas may be lit every year, but for some families, a loved one's absence remains impossible to ignore. And sometimes, the most painful part of a promise is not that it was forgotten, but that the person who made it never got the chance to keep it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Drone attack on Colombian army base kills three soldiers and wounds 16
articles.summary: Colombian President de la Espriella says those behind the attack in Santa Rosa del Sur will have ‘nowhere to hide’.
articles.body:
A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia has killed three soldiers and wounded at least 16, the country’s armed forces said.

The Colombian military said in a statement on Saturday that the attack hit a base in Santa Rosa del Sur, a small town in the foothills of the San Lucas mountain range. Authorities have not said who carried out the strike, the latest in a series of attacks on security forces as violence rises across rural parts of the country.

The area is rich in gold mines and has long been disputed by rebel armed groups including the Gulf Clan, the National Liberation Army (ELN) and smaller groups led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

Footage shared on social media showed clouds of smoke rising from the base after three explosions, and soldiers taking cover in shelters made of sandbags.

“Those who were behind this attack… will have nowhere to hide,” President Abelardo de la Espriella wrote on X. “Every attack against our soldiers strengthens our resolve to defend Colombia.”

Violence has intensified in several rural areas since de la Espriella, a conservative, took office in August.

The president cancelled peace talks with rebel groups and has taken a confrontational approach, including more air strikes, deploying more troops in some cities and creating joint task forces to defend strategic assets such as a pipeline that runs from the Caribbean coast to central Colombia.

De la Espriella’s government argues that armed groups used ceasefires granted by the previous government to consolidate their grip on rural areas, where they tax local businesses and profit from the drug trade.

Some groups have responded by stepping up attacks on the country’s armed forces.

Last week, a military base in Tolima province was targeted with missiles made from gas canisters. The attack killed four civilians, including a two-month-old baby.

Police in the border city of Cucuta have been attacked several times with remotely activated bombs.

State forces and illegal armed groups carried out 34 attacks with bombs or explosives in Colombia in the four weeks to October 16, a 9 percent increase on last year’s four-week average, according to ACLED, a group that monitors armed conflicts.

A 2016 peace deal with FARC led to the demobilisation of more than 14,000 fighters, but smaller groups have since fought over the rebels’ former territory.

articles.title: The Woodstock museum ensuring that we shall remember them
articles.summary: Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum staff and researchers share stories about Oxfordshire war heroes.
articles.body:
Once a year we promise ourselves to remember them and help their memory live on.

On Remembrance Sunday, the country honours those who died while serving in the armed forces.

In Woodstock, the Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum (SOFO) is home to exhibitions, memorabilia, archives and stories that reflect the breadth of the county's military history.

Here are stories from its staff, researchers and veterans that you could learn about and experience when visiting this museum on the edge of the Cotswolds.

"When we first opened the museum we were trying to gather as many news stories as we could and this is my absolute favourite story even 12 years on," says SOFO director Ursula Corcoran.

Charles Oliver Stone was an Oxfordshire man whose family emigrated to Australia when he was quite young, but when World War One was declared, he came back and joined the 69th Australian squadron of the Royal Flying Corps.

"He did his training at Queen's College in Oxford and he did many training flights out of London and one day in 1917, he was on his biplane and he crashed into a field of Brussels sprouts," Corcoran says.

"One of the farmer's daughters, Poppy, came out and Charles Stone got out of the biplane and this fantastic romance bloomed between the two of them."

Corcoran said: "He's documented as a World War One flying ace - not only was he bombing certain sites, but he was also getting into aerial combat, and we know that he got into aerial combat with the Red Baron".

Listen to the latest news from Oxfordshire

Researcher Trent Harron says the connection between James Bond author Ian Fleming's family and the museum is "very strong".

"[His father] Valentine Fleming was a Member of Parliament for the Division of Henley leading up to World War One and also a member of the Queen's Own Oxfordshire Hussars (QOOH).

"He was not only a remarkable statesman, but also an accomplished soldier and one who was revered by his peers and by the soldiers in the unit."

"Valentine's brother, Philip Fleming, who he served with in the QOOH, survived the war and went on to establish a charitable fund which largely contributed to the museum's foundation."

Harron says Valentine Fleming and Winston Churchill were "close friends" and when Fleming died on 20 May 1917, Churchill wrote an appreciation.

"This news will arouse sorrow in Oxfordshire and in the House of Commons," it read.

"Alert, methodical, resolute, untiring, he did his work, whether perilous or dull, without the slightest sign of strain or stress to the end."

SOFO marketing manager Duncan Parsons has a personal connection to the museum.

He says his great uncle, William Charles Parsons, took part in the third and final airborne operation on D-Day, Operation Mallard.

"He died of wounds on 20 June, so he was likely a casualty to that."

"As a kid, we would still go over to Normandy and see the graves and we'd always be going out to military museums - it was always something that felt present with the family."

Blenheim Palace social historian Antonia Keaney, whose husband is chair of SOFO's trustees, says she first came across World War Two's Spitfire Woman Molly Rose through her granddaughter.

"[She] used to babysit for my children when they were little and I hadn't realised at the time quite what a special woman she was," Keaney said.

Through her work, she learned that at the end of WW2 there were more than 600 Spitfires found on Blenheim land and that there used to be a runway.

Molly Rose, originally from Cambridgeshire, developed a fascination for flying from her older brother who could fly and had an aircraft "tethered in their back garden".

When the war broke out, pilots were needed not only for conflict, but also for transportation.

"That's where Molly Rose came into her own - she had a pilot's licence, and she was one of the girls that used to fly planes from A to B," Keaney said.

Damaged aircraft such as Spitfires and Hurricanes were then taken to the Cowley Works for repair.

The historian says she recently read that throughout the entire period the women "shifted over 300,000 planes or they made over 300,000 flights".

"One of the things I also find really remarkable about women like Molly Rose is that they were actually in quite great danger and they knew there was a certain risk attached to it," she added.

"Go to St Aldate's police station and ask to see the John Howard memorial they've got," says former SOFO trustee David Innes.

He says the exploits of Major John Howard and his men "are still very fondly and very warmly regarded"

He led men from the Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry to seize Pegasus Bridge over the Caen canal on D-Day in the Coup de Main Operation.

Innes says that thanks to the Coup de Main group "the eastern flank of the invasion was secured early on and made it much more difficult for the Germans to reinforce their positions above the beaches".

Starting as an Oxford City policeman, Major Howard joined the army when the threat of war started to loom.

"He very quickly proved himself to be an aggressive and determined and a man for detail," Innes says.

Later, Major Howard was wounded and was involved in a "really horrific road traffic accident, which largely immobilised him".

"But he was a great character, he was very fondly regarded by his men," Innes says.

"We go back with his family every year to Pegasus Bridge to mark the anniversary of D-Day.

"We've now marked 82 years since those days and the name John Howard is on everyone's lips when we go over there."

articles.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh, Eastern province
articles.summary: The interceptions come as the Houthis report 33 people killed in a coalition air attack on a village near Sanaa.
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis says its air defences have destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by the Iran-aligned armed group towards the kingdom.

Two of the missiles were launched towards the kingdom’s capital, Riyadh, Major-General Turki al-Maliki, the coalition’s spokesperson, said in a post on X on Sunday.

Later, the coalition said it intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles in Riyadh and the southern region.

Earlier, al-Maliki also confirmed another interception of a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards the kingdom’s Eastern province.

The attacks come as fighting intensifies across Yemen between the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), and government forces, who launched the Dawn of Yemen operation aimed at retaking Houthi-held territory, including the capital, Sanaa, last month.

The Houthi-run Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees al-Asbahi, said on Saturday that 33 people, including eight women and 13 children, were killed after Saudi-led coalition air attacks on the village of al-Shariyah, near Sanaa.

In a post on X, al-Asbahi said at least 39 others were wounded in the attacks on Saturday, which targeted homes, roads, paramedics and civil defence teams in the village, located in the Bani Hushaish district east of Sanaa.

There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition on the reported strikes. Al Jazeera could not independently verify the reports.

Media outlets affiliated with the Houthis reported on Sunday that various areas of the Shada border district in Saada province have also been subjected to artillery shelling.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree earlier claimed that the coalition had carried out 105 air strikes and missile attacks over 24 hours targeting Sanaa and seven other governorates, taking the total number of strikes since the escalation began to 4,369.

The Houthis, meanwhile, carried out six operations targeting Aramco oil facilities, Riyadh airport and Saudi military positions on both sides of the border, Saree claimed in a post on X.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province killed 30 people. The Houthis blamed it on Saudi air strikes, while Yemeni government forces accused the Iran-aligned group of firing a ballistic missile at the site.

According to the United Nations, more than 1,600 people have been killed and almost 300,000 displaced since a 2022 ceasefire collapsed in July after the Houthis announced a blockade of Saudi ports.

In September, the Houthis seized much of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive, while government forces launched a campaign to reclaim Houthi-held territory in October.

She didn’t want Blanchard to get any kind of momentum that was going to put her away. Blanchard caught Keyra with a thrust kick and hit a DDT to put Keyra away. Blanchard made clear she was putting the rest of the MLW women’s division on notice. Shotzi Blackheart is currently the MLW women’s world champion but there’s a whole host of women on the roster gunning for her. Blanchard is far from the only one but her momentum is building. The rest of the roster includes Scarlett Bordeaux, Zamaya and Masha. But you never know who else is going to "choose violence." articles.title: Over 40 fire calls on Diwali; major blazes reported in Khandsa, Sector 67 in Gurgaon
articles.summary: Gurgaon fire department received 42 Diwali fire calls; major blazes in Khandsa Road, DLF Phase 4 and Sector 67, with no casualties reported.
articles.body: Gurgaon: The fire department received 42 fire calls across the city on Sunday during Diwali celebrations, with most incidents involving scrap shops and waste dumps. Fire officials said several fires were also reported at residential properties, commercial establishments and markets.No casualties were reported, fire officials said, adding that sparks from firecrackers were suspected to have caused most of the fires.Among the major incidents, a hardware store on Khandsa Road caught fire around 2.50pm. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot, and it took nearly three hours to bring the blaze under control. The exact cause is being investigated, though sparks from firecrackers have not been ruled out, an official said.Another major fire broke out around 8.30pm on the ground floor of a four-storey building at Orchid Crescent in DLF Phase 4. Preliminary findings suggested that a short circuit in the building’s electrical panel triggered the blaze.Sparks quickly turned into flames, engulfing the panel and spreading to parts of the ground floor. Thick smoke filled the premises, prompting residents to evacuate. Firefighters and police rushed to the spot and contained the blaze before it could spread to the upper floors or adjoining houses.In another incident, a house on the second floor of a residential society in Sector 67 caught fire. Two fire tenders were deployed. The occupants were not at home when the blaze broke out, leaving the house completely gutted. “Firecracker sparks are suspected to have triggered the fire, though the exact cause is yet to be ascertained,” the official said.Several commercial establishments and scrap shops also caught fire during the day. A shop in Sadar market caught fire, triggering panic in the busy market, while another blaze was reported at J Tower in Police Lines. Firefighters brought both incidents under control.In Arjun Nagar, a scrap shop caught fire, with stored waste and plastic items allowing the flames to spread rapidly. A shop opposite Krishna Palace in Nai Basti also caught fire. In Rajiv Nagar, Sector 13, a fire at a bicycle shop damaged several bicycles and other goods. Firefighters were also called to a scrap shop near Jodi village, as well as to incidents in Palam Vihar and Udyog Vihar. A cycle shop in Sector 13 was also engulfed in flames.A fire official said the Sector 29 fire station received around 15 calls on Sunday. articles.title: Chiefs' failed trade deadline pursuit reveals a major roster concern
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs may have missed filling one roster gap.
articles.body:
The NFL deadline is officially over, and the Kansas City Chiefs walked out of the room with an important new wide receiver in Josh Downs. The team has a lot to be happy about when it comes to this pickup, but they're still not quite a perfect squad.

Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano of ESPN have released a feature offering up reactions to some of the trades that happened as the trade deadline hit. In the piece, they offer up some inside information on the Chiefs.

"The Chiefs' search for a wide receiver came down to the wire," Fowler said. "As of last week, the leaguewide sentiment was the Chiefs were willing to part with a fourth-round pick for Josh Downs. But Indianapolis held out for more, even waiting until around 3:30 p.m. ET Tuesday to finally consummate the deal."

He adds, "The belief is that Indy wanted a third-round pick. It eventually got fourth- and fifth-rounders in exchange for Downs and a seventh-round selection."

Kansas City Chiefs may still have a weakness at cornerback

While it's great that the Chiefs got Downs, they missed out on improving another area of their lineup. Fowler reports that the team wanted to improve their cornerback situation but came out of the trade deadline empty-handed.

"The Chiefs also had interest in Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr. but were told no by the Jaguars . And the Chiefs also looked at the cornerback market but ultimately didn't do a deal there," he notes.

So, if there's a weakness still in this lineup, and that's an if, it's certainly at cornerback. But this team still has a lot to smile about having Downs in the fold.

articles.title: Colombia: Eight killed in air strike targeting Gulf Clan gang
articles.summary: A suspected gang leader considered a "priority target" was among those killed, the Colombian president says.
articles.body:
A senior leader of Colombia's largest criminal gang, the Gulf Clan, is among eight people killed in an air strike carried out by the country's armed forces, according to President Abelardo de la Espriella.

De la Espriella said he had personally authorised the bombing targeting the Gulf Clan in the province of Antioquia, in north-west Colombia.

He added that Haminton Mosquera, whom he described as a senior member of the crime gang and one of 10 "priority targets" for Colombia's security forces, had been "brought down".

De la Espriella was elected in June after campaigning on a promise to crack down on Colombia's powerful criminal gangs, including by launching air strikes.

In a post on X , he said that Mosquera was suspected of having ordered attacks against the security forces, including the murder of a police officer in the municipality of Tarazá last year.

The Gulf Clan has been engaging in criminal activities for decades, mainly trafficking cocaine from Colombia to destinations in the US and Europe but also illegal mining and people smuggling.

The US added it to its list of Foreign Terrorist Organisations (FTOs) last year.

In his post, President de la Espriella said that "the offensive won't stop" and vowed to regain control of areas currently controlled by criminal organisations such as the Gulf Clan.

While his offensive against criminal gangs has been welcomed by many living in areas where extortion and gang violence are rampant, de la Espriella has faced criticism for the way he has made some of his announcements on security.

Less than a month after taking office, he published a video showing him walking among 23 body bags containing the remains of 23 people killed in an air strike on a suspected guerrilla camp.

On Wednesday, he shared a photo in which he can be seen writing his campaign slogan, "Welcome to the miracle homeland" on a bomb.

He has also defended his decision to wear an army uniform at a recent event in Cúcuta at which he confronted a detainee suspected of being a Farc rebel.

"What did you make of the bomb I sent you, signed by me?," the president can be heard asking the man.

He later told journalists that he wore the uniform because "I am a soldier of the homeland. That's why I dress like a soldier, because I came to serve Colombia. Because I honour the heroes, police officers and military."

Additional reporting by BBC Monitoring's Luis Fajardo.

articles.title: House passes Major Richard Star Act, sending bill to Senate
articles.summary: The House on Thursday passed legislation designed to allow combat-wounded medically retired veterans to receive retirement pay and disability compensation simultaneously without facing any penalties. articles.body:
The House on Thursday passed legislation designed to allow combat-wounded medically retired veterans to receive retirement pay and disability compensation simultaneously without facing any penalties.

The legislation, championed by House Veterans’ Affairs Committee ranking member Mark Takano (D-Calif.), was brought to the floor after Democrats successfully garnered 218 signatures on a discharge petition to force a vote on the bill. It passed the lower chamber by a vote of 392-18.

Under a longstanding federal policy, veterans who have medically retired because of combat-related injuries cannot receive the full amounts of both their military retirement pay and disability compensation because of mandatory offsets.

But this measure would eliminate that rule, which many veteran advocacy groups and lawmakers have dubbed the “wounded veteran tax.”

“Combat-wounded veterans who were forced to medically retire are being shortchanged by the VA [Department of Veterans Affairs],” Rep. Raul Ruiz (D-Calif.), who co-authored the bill with Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-Fla.), said in a statement . “For every dollar in VA disability compensation these veterans receive, a dollar is taken out of their retirement pay.”

He added, “Our veterans deserve respect, they do NOT deserve to be treated like a burdensome, expendable line item in a budget.”

The bill, dubbed the Major Richard Star Act, was named after a U.S. Army combat engineer who was diagnosed with cancer following toxic burn pit exposure.

Takano said on the House floor Wednesday that it is “far past time for us to end the wounded warrior tax and to give our combat-wounded veterans the compensation they have earned.”

Bilirakis did not sign the discharge petition to bring the bill to the floor. He has instead praised Republicans for including the Major Richard Star Act in a broader partisan legislative package, dubbed the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (TCAVA) that passed the House by voice vote Wednesday. Democrats have opposed the TCAVA because they argue it would expand some veterans’ benefits by slashing others.

The Major Richard Star Act, which was originally introduced in 2023, has been supported by a variety of veterans groups, but its potential passage had been blocked by Republican senators in 2025 and earlier this year over cost concerns. The Major Richard Star Act received a boost earlier this year after being endorsed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

The bill could face an uphill climb in the Senate, however, where fiscal hawk conservatives have aired concerns about the lack of offsets.
